description: What each identity may and may not do. This file is the policy; the proof makes Azure agree with it. A change here is a change to who can do what, and shows up in review as one.

probes.why: Reading is the entire purpose of this identity.
listKeys is an action, not a read. A Reader that can call it holds the data, and people assume it cannot.

probes.action: write a tag on the resource group
probes.why: The smallest possible write. If this succeeds, the role is not read-only.
Any identity that can do this is an administrator regardless of what its role is called.
An operator that cannot see the estate cannot operate it.
Needed to know what it is looking at.
Restarting a service never requires its data keys.

probes.action: write a tag on the resource group
probes.why: Restart is an action on a running thing, not permission to change it.
Same as every other identity here.
Contributor genuinely can, which is worth knowing rather than assuming it cannot.

probes.action: write a tag on the resource group
probes.why: Building infrastructure is what this identity is for.
The boundary that matters. Contributor is widely treated as safe because it cannot grant access, and this is the assertion that keeps that true.
